sections.html:
Washington County's seat sits in the Ozarks where the Boston Mountains begin. Fayetteville had 93,949 people at the 2020 census and an estimated 106,623 in July 2025, ranking second among Arkansas cities by size.

The terrain shapes what buyers worry about. Steep driveways, slopes, retaining walls and aging foundations, particularly on Mount Sequoyah and around the Square, draw closer scrutiny than a flat lot would. If your lot has any of these, dig up the paperwork for past foundation or wall repairs before you list.

On a sloped lot the inspector will walk the drainage first: where roof water goes, whether the grade tips toward the foundation, and whether a retaining wall leans or cracks. Older foundations near the Square get the same attention. None of this kills a sale, but a buyer who finds a surprise will usually ask for a lower price or a repair credit. If you know about a problem, say so in the first conversation. A cash buyer can price a known issue into the offer, while a lender-financed buyer may need it fixed before the loan funds.

The University of Arkansas is the largest employer in town and the strongest pull on housing demand. Enrollment topped 29,000 in fall 2021, a record then. Washington Regional Medical Center, Walmart and the school district round out the biggest payrolls. Walmart and J.B. Hunt have headquarters nearby, and Tyson is based in neighboring Springdale.

Corporate jobs across the region supply home buyers, while the campus supplies tenants. Owners of student rentals frequently sell once a lease ends or a unit has sat empty, because showing a vacant place mid-semester is a hassle.

Three areas are named historic districts: Wilson Park, Mount Nord and Washington-Willow. Homes in those districts may face design expectations from the city and neighbors, so talk to the planning office before you repaint, re-side or rebuild a porch to prepare for a sale.

Fayetteville Public Schools runs eight elementary schools, four intermediate schools, two special schools and Fayetteville High School. Parents often look up attendance zones first, so note the schools assigned to your address and verify them with the district. Some edges of town may fall in other districts, and the district office can settle it.

Check each district's boundaries against the address on the deed, since a buyer may ask for it in writing. Putting the school names in your listing notes saves time later.

Interstate 49 carries US 71 and is the main way through town. It was I-540 until the I-49 designation was approved on March 28, 2014. College Avenue, once US 71B, remains the commercial spine. Many listings mention the Razorback Greenway, a 36-mile mostly off-road trail linking Fayetteville with Bella Vista by way of Johnson, Springdale, Lowell, Bentonville and Rogers. Northwest Arkansas National Airport is roughly 17 miles to the northwest.

Summer highs average about 89 degrees and winter lows about 27, with around 47 inches of precipitation yearly. After a hard winter, pipes in unheated crawlspaces and older roofs are where trouble tends to show. Inspectors and buyers ask about the roof, the HVAC unit and the water heater, so keep receipts and install dates on hand.

Renting a home by the night in Fayetteville requires a city permit, and the city defines two kinds. Type I covers a home where full-time occupants live on the property and rent out a room or addition. Type II covers a place where guests stay nightly and nobody lives there full time. Applicants have needed a business license, a building safety inspection, proof of ownership, an insurance review, sales tax filings and a listing on the landlord registry.

When you own a permitted rental, ask the planning office whether the permit transfers to a buyer before you promise it as part of the sale.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
The Washington County collector bills real estate tax, and payment is due October 15 every year. Pay later and a 10% penalty applies, along with 10% annual interest. Online payment by credit card carries a processing fee. You can also pay at the office or mail a check following the directions printed on your annual statement. Questions about a statement go to 479-444-1526.

Your title company will work out how the current year's bill is split at closing. On top of that, Arkansas charges a real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of the price, run by the state Department of Finance and Administration.

Owing tax does not rule out a sale. The balance, with its penalty and interest, comes out of your proceeds at the closing table. Call the collector for today's figure and pass it to the title company early so the payoff is already on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Steps to sell a Fayetteville house
sections.html: Begin with the paperwork: your tax statement, any rental permit records, a payoff figure from your mortgage company, and the names on the deed. Next, decide how fast you need to close. Then request offers in writing and compare each one by the money you would actually keep. Once you accept, the title company opens the file, checks ownership and liens, and sets the closing date. On closing day the tax split, any payoff and the transfer tax are all settled on one statement.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a Fayetteville owner?
sections.html:
Cash works for owners who value certainty above the best possible price. Common cases include a house that needs work the owner cannot pay for, an inherited home still in another person's name, a landlord getting out of rentals, and a move with a firm date.

A listing in a busy market might bring more, but only after repairs, showings and the buyer's financing all line up. A cash offer gives up part of that upside for a closing date you can plan around, and it avoids the appraisal and lender repair demands that so often cause delay or a renegotiated price.

One more point for landlords: a tenant in place limits what a buyer can do with the house. Share the lease terms and rent early, and note any short-term rental permit so buyers know what they are getting.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell a short-term rental in Fayetteville?
faqs.a: You need no permit to sell, but permit status matters to a buyer. Ask the city's planning office whether the permit stays with the property or the new owner must apply.

faqs.q: When are Washington County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment is due October 15 each year. Late payments draw a 10% penalty plus 10% annual interest.

faqs.q: What is the Arkansas transfer tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: The state charges $3.30 per $1,000 of the actual price on a deed that conveys real estate. Your purchase contract names the party who pays.

faqs.q: Is Fayetteville a good place to sell a rental near campus?
faqs.a: Demand from the University of Arkansas and regional employers helps. Timing matters, because a vacant unit is harder to show during the school year.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fayetteville house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can take it as it is. Get written offers and compare each with the net from a repaired listing.
